sources.note: A speculative-decoding rollout engine for RL post-training that keeps the target sampling distribution exact while adapting the drafter at two timescales.

result.definition: Proposing several tokens cheaply and verifying them against the target model, so that accepted proposals are generated in fewer forward passes without changing the output distribution. One source adapts it to RL training, where the target policy keeps changing so a static proposer goes stale, using lightweight future-token heads with fast hidden-state correction and slow head updates; exact target verification is what leaves the GRPO objective unchanged, so the 1.21-2.04x end-to-end speedup costs nothing in quality. The other reports improved speculative-decoding efficiency as a side effect of a hierarchical latent pretraining objective. Both treat exactness as the property that makes the speedup free rather than a trade-off.
